title: Pooled connections and why PreparedStatement repeats fast

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Code calls close() on a Connection it got from a HikariCP DataSource. What happens to that connection?

options.text: The network link to the database is shut, and the pool opens a new one for the next request.
options.says: Opening a connection costs a TCP handshake and a login each time, which is exactly the cost a pool exists to avoid.

options.text: It goes back to the pool's idle set, and a later getConnection() can hand it out again.
options.says: A pooled connection's close() returns it to the pool; the physical connection stays open for reuse.

options.text: It throws an exception, because a pooled connection is given back with a method of the pool.
options.says: Code releases a pooled connection with the ordinary close(), which is why try-with-resources works with a pool.

questions.stem: Why can a PreparedStatement run a query that is repeated many times faster than a Statement can?

options.text: The driver keeps the rows of the last run and returns them when the values match.
options.says: No result is reused: every execution runs the query against the current data.

options.text: The driver sends all runs to the database together in one network round trip.
options.says: That describes batching with addBatch() and executeBatch(), a separate feature.

options.text: The database reuses the execution plan it built for the SQL with its ? placeholders.
options.says: The SQL text stays the same across runs, so the plan made once for it can be cached and reused.

concepts: A connection pool hands out reused connections and close() returns one to the pool instead of closing it; DataSource is preferred to DriverManager.
Statement runs static SQL, PreparedStatement parameterised SQL whose plan the database can cache, and CallableStatement stored procedures.
